webster.text: Want of that firmness and strength of mind which constitutes courage or fortitude; weakness of spirit; cowardliness; that feebleness of mind which shrinks from trifling or imaginary dangers.

example.quote: He had heard it surmised that ihe general government would probably never obhge the British to quit these posts ; but whcuiever, said he, I find the Union guilty of such pusillanimity, I shall regret that I ever drew my breath in this country.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 2, New York Convention, July 1, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
